summary: ExpenseBatch manages expense batch records, including creation, updating, searching, and deletion. It encapsulates the data structure and persistence logic for expense batches within the system.
purpose: To provide CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations and structure for expense batches, corresponding to workflow needs for department-level tracking and status management of expense batches.

fields.name: BatchDate
fields.description: The date the batch was created

fields.name: BatchNumberFormatted
fields.description: Formatted batch number for display, combining ID and status description

workflows.name: Search for Expense Batches
steps: Results are read and ExpenseBatch objects are constructed with ID, StatusCode, StatusDescription, BatchNumberFormatted.

workflows.name: Search ExpenseBatch by ID
steps: Retrieve batch fields: ID, DepartmentID, BatchDescription, BatchDate, StatusCodeID, StatusCode, StatusDescription (with language support), ClosedDate, BatchNumberFormatted.

workflows.name: Add ExpenseBatch
steps: Call ExpenseBatch.Add with session, departmentID, batchDescription, batchDate.
Procedure 'ExpenseBatchAdd' is invoked with specified parameters.

workflows.name: Update ExpenseBatch
steps: Call ExpenseBatch.Update with session, id, batchDescription, batchDate, statusCodeID.

workflows.name: Delete ExpenseBatch
steps: Call ExpenseBatch.Delete with session and id.

business_rules: StatusDescription is selected to use the alternate language field if language preferences are set.
BatchNumberFormatted combines ID and StatusDescription for display.
validations: All CRUD method calls rely on parameterized stored procedures, assuming DB-level validations on ID, departmentID, batchDescription, batchDate, statusCodeID.
conditions: If StatusDescriptionAlt is present and language preference is set, use it; otherwise, use StatusDescription.
system_behavior: All data access is through HSPnetSession's DB context and stored procedures.
ExpenseBatch objects are built from DB data and returned for use in application/UI.
dependencies: SQL stored procedures: ExpenseBatchSearch, ExpenseBatchSearchID, ExpenseBatchAdd, ExpenseBatchUpdate, ExpenseBatchDelete
exceptions: If no data is returned from the database (reader is null), methods return an empty list or default ExpenseBatch object.
All DB readers are properly closed after use.
content_gaps: No information about UI interactions or user-triggered validations.
No explicit business logic for edge cases (e.g., deletion of closed batches).
No detail on permissions or authorization checks.
